solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cut around bog's high ridge

indicators.note: the word for cut is placed around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: to hack is to cut roughly

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

explanation.surface: Someone clears a path round a marsh on the way up a ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: No clue word signals the scrambling of the marsh word; the setter leaves it unmarked, so treat that step as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogsback is a sharp-crested hill or ridge, named for its resemblance to a pig's spine.

clue.text: The sound of appealing gig

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that is said like the word for appealing

parts.note: appealing means good-looking, handsome

explanation.surface: A comment on how an attractive musical performance sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gig' looks like a concert but is a light two-wheeled carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a horse-drawn two-wheeled cab, a kind of light carriage like a gig.

clue.text: Miss sign probed by one scientist

indicators.note: the girl-and-sign pair has the letter for one pushed into it, as a probe enters

parts.note: a miss is a girl, a gal
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young woman's star sign is investigated by a researcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist who championed the telescope.

clue.text: Lovely creature's embraced with irritation

indicators.note: the creature word holds the other letters in its arms

parts.note: a creature is a being; the 's stands for 'has', a link
an itch is an irritation

explanation.surface: A charming animal is hugged despite an annoying itch.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewitching means enchantingly attractive, so it is a synonym of lovely in the charming sense.

clue.text: Church plugs device as a way to avoid issue

indicators.note: the church abbreviation fills a gap in the device word, like a plug in a hole

parts.note: a contraption is a gadget or device
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The Church promotes a gadget as a way of avoiding trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is offspring here, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth control is the means by which couples avoid having children, issue being an old word for offspring.

clue.text: What arithmetician does is brood at university

parts.note: a brood of children are tots
to be up is to be in residence at university, in British usage

explanation.surface: A mathematician's activity is said to be sulking while at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brood' is a noun (a family of young children), not the verb to sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone doing sums adds figures to reach a total, which is the phrasal verb here.

clue.text: War writer's love novel rejected

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for novel is turned round in this down clue

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: A war author's romance novel was turned down by publishers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilfred Owen was the First World War poet of Dulce et Decorum Est, so a war writer.

clue.text: Posed a gripping problem, something to get your teeth into!

definitions.text: something to get your teeth into!

indicators.note: the posed word with A holds the problem word tight inside

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose, so posed gives sat
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone set a riveting puzzle, a real challenge to tackle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a tough task but is literal: a fruit to bite into.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small citrus fruit, literally something you sink your teeth into.

clue.text: Knock up meat dish for a tale teller

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a rap is a knock
a doner kebab is a meat dish

explanation.surface: Instructions to quickly prepare a meaty meal for a storyteller.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pardoner is one of the pilgrims who tells a story in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Collar hasn't a zip

indicators.note: the word for collar does not have the letter A, so it is dropped

parts.note: to collar or nail someone is to catch or arrest them

explanation.surface: A shirt collar lacks a zip fastener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' is not a fastener but slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip is American slang for nothing, and nil means nothing or zero.

clue.text: Carbon in gas fire, something to keep out the chill

definitions.text: something to keep out the chill

indicators.note: the carbon symbol sits inside, between the two words

parts.note: wind is gas in the digestive sense
an electric or gas fire is a heater
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Carbon in a gas fire is what keeps the cold at bay.
explanation.definitionFit: A windcheater is a windproof jacket, worn to keep cold air out.

clue.text: One used to flog online business, blocking terrible sanction

indicators.note: the online business word blocks a gap in the jumbled letters by sitting inside them
terrible says the word sanction is mangled into a new order

parts.note: e-tail is retail done over the internet

explanation.surface: Someone trying to sell things on the internet is hampered by a dreadful penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flog' looks like sell, the online business of the surface, but here it means whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails was a knotted whip of nine cords used for flogging sailors and prisoners.

clue.text: Hide from man who's left school educated

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
literate means educated, able to read and write

explanation.surface: Someone ducks out of sight of a well-schooled former pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb meaning to conceal oneself from someone; it is the definition, meaning to blot out.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out or cover completely, so to hide from view.

clue.text: Victor, say, heading for upset after hard game

indicators.note: the first letter of upset comes after the hard abbreviation

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, taken from upset

parts.note: go is the Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A winner sets out to cause an upset after a tough match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a winner but is the French novelist's first name, so Victor is an example of someone surnamed Hugo.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo wrote Les Misérables, so Victor is one example of a Hugo.

clue.text: Playwright made great strides, European star

parts.note: loped means ran with long strides
Vega is the brightest star in Lyra

explanation.surface: A dramatist made big progress and became a European celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lope de Vega was the hugely prolific Spanish dramatist of the Golden Age.

clue.text: Understood this Latin building style

parts.note: to get something is to understand it, so understood gives got
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: Someone grasped this classical style of architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the medieval architectural style of pointed arches and flying buttresses.

clue.text: Scoffed after New Age's recent arrival

indicators.note: the eating word follows the other pieces

parts.note: an eon is an age; the 's stands for 'has', a link
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed gives ate

explanation.surface: Someone mocked a newcomer to the New Age movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' looks like mocked; here it means ate.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn baby, the most recent arrival of all.

clue.text: Cash reduced by bishops, for example

indicators.note: reduced says the cash word loses its last letter

parts.note: specie is money in coin
bishops are chessmen, so men

explanation.surface: Clergy are cutting their spending, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishops' are not clergy but chess pieces, men on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or instance taken as typical of its kind.

clue.text: Vent anger on school's Dickensian character

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the anger word comes after the school word

parts.note: a school of whales is a pod; the 's is a possessive link
to snap is to speak irritably

explanation.surface: A teacher loses their temper at a pupil's novel character.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Podsnap is the pompous complacent gentleman in Dickens's Our Mutual Friend.

clue.text: Characters in flannelette, cotton or natty jacket?

definitions.text: Characters in flannelette, cotton or natty
definitions.meaning: each of these words contains a repeated pair of the letter T
a close-fitting man's jacket of the Renaissance period

explanation.definitionFit: A doublet was the snug padded jacket worn by men in Tudor times; split, it reads as a double letter T.

clue.text: Conflict not required to see off a group of Nazis

indicators.note: to see someone off is to get rid of them, so these letters are removed

parts.note: needless means not required
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A war was unnecessary to defeat a band of Nazis.
explanation.definitionFit: Needle is British slang for hostility or rivalry, as in a needle match between bitter rivals.

clue.text: Its role is to reform lags?

indicators.note: to reform something is to form it anew, so the letters are remade into a new order

explanation.surface: A prison's purpose is to rehabilitate convicts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lags' looks like the British slang noun for convicts but is a verb, dawdles.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag is to fall behind or dawdle, which is what someone who hangs about does.

clue.text: Leave pastry wraps and an amount of drink

indicators.note: the pastry word wraps around the leaving word

parts.note: a flan is a pastry case with a filling
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Instructions to leave the pastry wrapped, with something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel for wine or cider, or the quantity of drink it holds.

clue.text: Novice boxes in learner driver?

indicators.note: the novice word encloses the learner letter

parts.note: a cub is a beginner, as in cub reporter
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A beginner hems in a learner motorist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' looks like a motorist but is a golf club, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is the golf club used for long tee shots, so it is one example of a club.

clue.text: Seizure by police to get the job done

parts.note: a fit is a seizure
the Bill, short for Old Bill, is British slang for the police

explanation.surface: A suspect's fit while under arrest got the work finished.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be exactly what is needed, suitable for the purpose.

clue.text: Cut a couple of diamonds

parts.note: a couple of means diamonds is to be taken in two senses; D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jeweller cuts a pair of gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of' says diamonds is used twice: D (the suit abbreviation) and ICE (slang).
explanation.definitionFit: To dice is to cut food into small cubes.

clue.text: The writer's going to island covered in mud — he's rolling in it

indicators.note: the writer and island pieces are covered by the mud word, inside it

parts.note: mire is mud or bog
the writer is I, and I will gives the contraction I'll
Iona is a Hebridean island

explanation.surface: An author heads to a muddy island, happily wallowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling in it' suggests wallowing in mud; it is the idiom for very rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling in it is an idiom for being extremely wealthy, describing someone with a fortune.

clue.text: Some work accordingly isn't finished

indicators.note: the word for accordingly loses its final letter

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, accordingly

explanation.surface: A remark that a piece of work is still incomplete.
explanation.definitionFit: The erg is a small unit of work or energy in the CGS system.

clue.text: Lower number follows unspecified one

indicators.note: the numbing word follows the unspecified number

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths
a number is something that numbs, and ether is an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A smaller figure comes after an indefinite one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as numb-er, an anaesthetic, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or under, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: A sauce eaten by wrong butcher?

indicators.note: the sauce word is swallowed inside the wrong word

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
sauce is cheek or impudence, sass

explanation.surface: A dressing is consumed by a misguided meat seller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' as a verb means kill brutally; the noun here is a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A butcher in the figurative sense slaughters people, which is what a hired killer does.
